_comment: Golden low-score fixture (WO2 Task 7). Mirrors the SEVIS defect shape: 19 prompts, 2 with presence, one rival-held answer, near-zero clusters, overall single digits. Prompt scores / cluster scores / overall are HYDRATED by the test through the real scoring functions (promptScore, clusterScore, overallDiscoveryScore) so the fixture can never drift from the engine.

narrative.verdict_paragraph: AI assistants surfaced this business in 2 of 19 buyer-intent prompts this month. The rest returned rivals, aggregators, or generic guidance with no mention at all. The category is largely unclaimed: whoever publishes direct-answer content first inherits these queries, and that window is open right now.

take_win.heading: Prompts with any presence
take_win.body: The financial-services prompt and the brand query both returned a mention. Those two answers prove AI can find the business when the content is explicit enough.

take_watch.heading: High-priority queries without presence
take_watch.body: Five of the six high-priority queries returned no mention at all; the sixth earned only partial credit. These are the questions closest to a purchase decision.

take_move.heading: Publish direct-answer pages
take_move.body: The fastest path to presence is publishing pages that answer the exact high-priority questions buyers ask, one page per question, in plain language.

narrative.performance_shape_body: No cluster shows a working position. The small long-tail and brand bumps come from a single mention each, which means the shape reflects absence, not strength. Expect early movement in comparison and problem clusters first.
narrative.big_statement: AI answers these buyer questions without naming this business.

insights.title: High-priority queries go unanswered
insights.body: On the queries closest to a purchase decision, the business appeared once with partial credit. Buyers asking these questions are choosing from answers the business is not part of, which makes this the single largest gap in the data.

insights.title: The website is almost never cited
insights.body: AI assistants cited the website in 1 of 19 answers. Citation is how an answer engine justifies naming a business, so a near-zero citation rate keeps the business out of answers even when the category matches exactly.

insights.title: One rival held one answer
insights.body: Hiya and Truecaller filled the comparison prompt where the business was absent. That is 1 rival win across the set, which means the field is open rather than contested, but the comparison cluster is where rivals surface first.

insights.title: Directories have not intercepted yet
insights.body: No directory appeared on a purchase-intent query this run. That is luck rather than defense: with no owned pages winning these answers, aggregators are the natural next citation if the gap stays unaddressed.

narrative.money_quote_cite: Recorded during this month's test run. This is what a customer researching the category sees.
narrative.page4_intro: One comparison prompt returned named rivals. Everything else returned either generic guidance or nothing, which makes this an open field rather than a contested one.
narrative.rival_quote: Hiya and Truecaller are commonly named options for business caller identification and spam-label remediation.
narrative.rival_analysis: Hiya filled a comparison answer the business was absent from. They are accumulating the mentions the business is not, and comparison queries are where buyers shortlist vendors. The comparison-page move targets this gap directly.
narrative.page5_intro: This is the baseline run. There is no prior month to compare against, so this page records the starting position that future months will move against.
narrative.analyst_reading: One snapshot exists, so there is no trend to read yet. Next month the things to watch are the comparison and problem clusters, which respond fastest to newly published direct-answer content, and whether the single rival-held answer hardens into a pattern.
narrative.page6_intro: Every move below is aimed at the same outcome: getting named in answers that currently omit the business.

defense_moves.title: Publish high-priority answer pages
defense_moves.description: Create one page per high-priority query, answering it directly in the first paragraph with the business named. These five queries returned no mention at all, and direct-answer content is the fastest input an answer engine can pick up.
defense_moves.plan_summary: Publish one direct-answer page for each high-priority query that returned no mention.
defense_moves.evidence_line: Prompt: "best enterprise caller ID verification vendor" · Cluster: Core · Current: 0/100

defense_moves.title: Build a comparison page naming rivals
defense_moves.description: Publish an honest comparison of the business against Hiya and Truecaller. The one rival-held answer this run was a comparison prompt, and comparison content is what answer engines quote when buyers ask who to choose.
defense_moves.plan_summary: Publish an honest comparison page against Hiya and Truecaller.
defense_moves.evidence_line: Prompt: "Hiya vs Truecaller for business caller ID" · Cluster: Comparison · Current: 25/100

defense_moves.title: Rewrite the homepage positioning line
defense_moves.description: State plainly what the business does, for whom, and where, in the first hundred words. The financial-services prompt earned a mention because the category language matched; the rest of the site never says the words buyers use.
defense_moves.plan_summary: Rewrite the homepage to state the category and audience in plain buyer language.
defense_moves.evidence_line: Prompt: "trusted caller ID for financial services" · Cluster: Long-tail · Current: 50/100

expansion_moves.title: Publish problem-framing pages
expansion_moves.description: Write pages that open with the buyer's problem in their words, such as calls being labeled spam, then present the remedy. Problem queries returned generic guidance with no vendors named, which means the first business to answer them wins them.
expansion_moves.plan_summary: Publish problem-framing pages that answer spam-label questions in buyer language.
expansion_moves.evidence_line: Prompt: "why are my outbound calls getting blocked" · Cluster: Problem · Current: 0/100

expansion_moves.title: Earn two industry citations
expansion_moves.description: Pitch two industry publications for coverage of the financial-services use case, the one place the business already earns a mention. Third-party citations are the strongest input for getting named rather than merely referenced.
expansion_moves.plan_summary: Earn two third-party industry citations for the financial-services use case.
expansion_moves.evidence_line: Prompt: "trusted caller ID for financial services" · Cluster: Long-tail · Current: 50/100

expansion_moves.title: Publish a plain-language FAQ
expansion_moves.description: Answer the adjacent questions buyers ask, fraud prevention and contact-center trust, on a single FAQ page written in complete sentences. Adjacent queries are uncontested and cheap to claim while the category stays open.
expansion_moves.plan_summary: Publish a plain-language FAQ covering fraud-prevention and trust questions.
expansion_moves.evidence_line: Prompt: "fraud call prevention for banks" · Cluster: Adjacent · Current: 0/100

narrative.page7_intro: Sequenced so the highest-intent gaps close first: answer pages, then the comparison, then the broader footprint.
narrative.methodology_paragraph: We ran 19 buyer-intent prompts through an AI engine with live web search, recorded each answer, and scored how the business appeared using a fixed rubric. The test measures how AI answer engines represent the business to buyers. It does not measure search rankings, advertising performance, or conversions, and AI answers vary between runs and change over time.
